book_xi_salt_road.label: BOOK XI
book_xi_salt_road.title: Water for the names that stayed

yuan_lian.name: Yuan Lian
yuan_lian.title: Forewoman of the valley water mill

salt_from_public.speaker: narrator
salt_from_public.text: The valley's commission packet reached Yue in a dry wind three weeks after the storm inquiry. She had permission to carry the commission's limited ledger extract; the original remained with its keeper. Duan Zhi's letter waited beside it. Salt Lantern Valley needed paid hands to inspect its water channels before the autumn rains. On the back, Su Lan had written a second request: bring enough patience to meet people who remembered Yue's first visit differently.

salt_public_002.speaker: lin_yue
salt_public_002.text: 'I can compare what this extract actually says,' Yue told the receiving clerk. 'The storm case does not certify every contract that mentions its fund.' She wrapped it again before taking the ordinary road. Once she had wanted a document powerful enough to settle a room when she entered it. Now she knew how easily people could give a seal that power without reading the words beneath it.

salt_public_003.speaker: narrator
salt_public_003.text: At the valley toll shelter, she ate millet before opening the map. The lake road had been checked for loaded carts that morning; the low marsh spur was still closed to wheels. Her fourth-stage cord carried no travel exemption. She paid the posted fare and asked whether the commission's promised return allowance covered a delayed departure. The clerk found the answer in the letter, then pointed her toward Su Lan's tower.

salt_from_workshop.speaker: narrator
salt_from_workshop.text: Three weeks after the storm inquiry, the repaired bell relay lay in its own padded case. It belonged to the workshop, which had loaned it for a timed demonstration at Salt Lantern Valley. Yue carried its signed condition sheet separately from the sample pack. Duan Zhi had asked for paid channel workers before the autumn rains. Su Lan's note added that a trustworthy bell could announce a turn, but could not decide who deserved one.

salt_workshop_002.speaker: su_lan
salt_workshop_002.text: 'Keep it on the public time circuit,' Su Lan said when the cases arrived. 'Nothing here will command the boundary through your borrowed relay.' She counted the seals with Yue, then sent the sample pack to its appointed cupboard. The bell keeper's hands had grown rougher since their last meeting. She was proud of the repaired tower roof and irritated by the leaking cistern behind it. Both feelings survived the welcome.

salt_workshop_003.speaker: narrator
salt_workshop_003.text: They walked to the square while the courier took the cases inside. The relay would be tested on the dry bench before any scheduled use, and the workshop would receive it at the loan's end. In the street, a woman filled two jars from a cart whose water cost more than Yue's breakfast. Su Lan saw where Yue was looking. 'Yes,' she said. 'The households have their names. Water still arrives by an older list.'

salt_from_home.speaker: narrator
salt_from_home.text: Three weeks after the storm inquiry, Yue's mother laid her witnessed grain-house receipt beside the cooling kiln. Its seasonal water surcharge appeared against a zero-draw entry in the supplier's schedule. She permitted comparison of her own bill, not neighboring workers' accounts. Duan Zhi's paid valley commission offered a chance to ask the grain house about its rate. Yue packed the copied receipt after breakfast, leaving its ordinary original in the household drawer.

salt_home_002.speaker: yue_mother
salt_home_002.text: 'Do not make my little bill into a story about everyone,' her mother said. 'The charge may have an explanation. I want to hear it beside the actual draw.' Yue agreed. At the door, her mother straightened the shoulder seam on her coat, then stopped herself from tightening it further. The old damaged route had not improved with her daughter's fourth stage. A needle, a stool and shorter kiln shifts remained the useful accommodations.

salt_home_003.speaker: narrator
salt_home_003.text: On the hired cart, Yue held the receipt cover on her knees. Wanting her mother to be right felt different from knowing the merchant had done wrong. She practiced the difference by copying the quantity and the total into separate columns. Around the last bend the lake appeared lower than she remembered. White mineral marks climbed the landing stones. The driver pointed to the drinking-water cart and told her to keep the two supplies apart.

salt_arrival_001.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_001.text: Su Lan greeted her beneath the tower clock, where ordinary weights drove the hands. A basin caught drips from a shaded spout. Beside it, nineteen household names remained on the corrected land notice. Yue found Wei Xiu's among them without having to search a blank. Across the square, however, the water seller's board still counted those households under a faded heading: absent claims, allocation held. Su Lan watched her read both notices.

salt_arrival_002.speaker: su_lan
salt_arrival_002.text: 'Nobody has withdrawn the hearing's correction,' Su Lan said. 'Those families own their standing. The water book was copied from an older schedule and never received the same amendment. A clerk says the water is waiting for them somewhere. Another clerk says it was never drawn. Meanwhile they buy jars from the cart. We need to know which shortage is real before choosing whom to shout at.'

salt_arrival_003.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_003.text: At the council room, Duan Zhi rested his cane against the table instead of standing for the welcome. The paid commission ran for twenty-four days, including two inspection days and a three-day trial. Each worker had a wage, meals, a shaded rest place and a return fare. The village hired qualified masons for buried walls. Yue's contract covered observation, copying and prepared small controls; her two opened arm pairs did not qualify her to lift a cistern.

salt_arrival_004.speaker: duan_zhi
salt_arrival_004.text: 'The dry-season spring gives one hundred twenty counted jars each day,' Duan said. 'Drinking, cooking and the clinic require one hundred fifty. The reserve holds sixteen hundred forty. Each counted jar means ten litres on our checked measure. We subtract unusable bottom water and transfer loss before writing that number. The lake is brackish. A thousand jars must remain untouched unless the council declares a new emergency.'

salt_arrival_005.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_005.text: Three baskets stood by the map: household cups, sacks for salt wash and seed trays from the grain house. The clean spring had fed all three when the higher seasonal flow allowed it. A fourth basket held empty transport jars. Wei Jin moved that basket closer to his chair. Ferry washing was already using lake water. The porters needed drinking water like everyone else; a freight contract was not a mouth.

salt_arrival_006.speaker: wei_jin
salt_arrival_006.text: 'The salt cooperative has orders due in nine days,' he said. 'If they miss them, my boats can carry raw salt at a poorer price. Some workers will lose the better wage. The grain house wants clean water for its seed lot before the next sowing. Neither request is imaginary. But if we spend tomorrow's drinking supply to rescue this week's price, I will have something very heavy to explain at the landing.'

salt_arrival_007.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_007.text: An Ru arrived with two thin books rather than the valley's famous household ledger. One was the current water turn book; the other recorded purchases from the reserve. The old land originals stayed in the archive. She had brought certified public portions that named duties and quantities, with private household accounts covered. Yue noticed that the absent-claims column had survived four fresh bindings. Each copy had made the mistake look more settled.

salt_arrival_008.speaker: an_ru
salt_arrival_008.text: 'Restored standing and an unpaid water credit are separate facts,' An Ru said. 'We will not make a family prove its existence again. We do have to establish what was billed, delivered or withheld. The water clerk can answer the entries in his book. He cannot supply consent for a household's private account, and my seal cannot do it for him.'

salt_arrival_009.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_009.text: Wei Xiu spread a working map across the table. An old bypass ran from the spring head toward the reeds, then vanished beneath a stone approach built during the boundary dispute. Someone had drawn it as abandoned. That morning the landing crew had heard water beneath it. The sound did not tell them where it went. Xiu marked the listening point and left the channel's far end blank.

salt_arrival_010.speaker: wei_xiu
salt_arrival_010.text: 'You can hear it from the public path,' she said. 'No digging yet. The bank holds houses as well as water. I would like you to remember that I am the person who pilots the boat there, even if the erased-name story makes a more interesting introduction. My land record came back. My customers did not all come back with it.'

salt_arrival_011.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_011.text: Yue began to answer with an apology for the years of loss, then realized she did not know which years Xiu meant. Instead she asked which customers had stopped coming and which trips still paid. Xiu pointed to two stopped freight runs. Their owners had moved while the dispute continued. A repaired notice could not compel them to return. The silence that followed was specific enough to be useful.

salt_arrival_012.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_012.text: The commission posted its temporary rule outside: essential jars first, ordinary collection points open to every restored household, optional industrial use paused for two days while the channel crew inspected. The salt foreman protested the pause. Duan invited him to record the expected lost wash batches, then signed his own responsibility for the inspection delay. The protest stayed on the board beneath the rule. Nobody had to call it agreement.

salt_arrival_013.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_013.text: That evening, Yue carried a clean cup to the tower stair and found Su Lan counting wick oil. Lantern maintenance still needed ordinary purchases. The bell keeper had refused to make shelter conditional on surrendering household records; lamp oil and ward-stone replacements still had their own costs. A young tower worker had left after the roof repair ended. Su Lan was doing his extra evening round until the village could pay another person.

salt_arrival_014.speaker: lin_yue
salt_arrival_014.text: 'When I left, I imagined the returned names would make things simpler,' Yue said. Su Lan kept counting. 'They made one wrong less defensible. We still needed to buy oil.' Yue watched the last drop slide from the measure. She had returned wanting to recognize her earlier work. Recognizing the labor after it might prove harder, because most of it had never belonged to her.

salt_arrival_015.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_015.text: At supper, the grain-house steward described seed mildew without asking the table to admire a harvest that had not happened. A salt worker showed his split thumbnail and the tally for nine lost washing shifts. A woman from one restored household brought the price of a cart jar. Each fact needed a place on the same plan. Yue put down her spoon before copying the first one, and Su Lan told her to finish eating.

salt_arrival_016.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_016.text: On the first inspection morning, Duan repeated Yue's permitted closure on the dry bench. Her first pair and second pair each carried their existing bounded test separately, with full discharge between them. No symptom required withdrawal. She then put the instrument away. The day's survey could be done with a level staff, chalk and a jar. She had once feared such a day wasted cultivation. Here it would test whether she could notice what cultivation did not measure.

salt_arrival_017.speaker: duan_zhi
salt_arrival_017.text: 'Choose where you can do the most attentive work,' Duan said. 'My channel crew, An Ru's accounts team and Xiu's household listeners will all bring reports. Taking one route does not give you the others' private pages. Before the council decides, we will hear each team's public findings and limits. I have signed for enough staff that your choice does not leave a channel unattended.'

salt_arrival_018.speaker: narrator
salt_arrival_018.text: Yue stood at the room's three doorways with a copied map in her hand. One led toward water under stone, another toward purchases that might have paid for nothing, the third toward people who were tired of proving they were thirsty. She could not repair all three by being conspicuously earnest. She could take a task seriously enough that someone else could build on its result.

salt_investigation_choice.speaker: lin_yue
salt_investigation_choice.text: 'I will work where I can ask a useful question and carry a checked answer back,' Yue said. The channel crew had a dry approach; the accounts team had public purchase entries; the household team had invitations that could be declined. Each route would change whom she spent these two days beside. The commission would still hear all three reports before opening an optional water turn.

choices.text: Inspect the bypass with Duan Zhi's channel crew.
Compare reserve purchases with An Ru's account team.
Listen to household water collectors with Wei Xiu.

salt_channels_001.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_001.text: At the watermill, an unused wheel cast thin shadows across the canal. Duan asked the miller to shut the mill race with its ordinary gate while the crew inspected the public bypass. The miller wanted the shutdown dated; flour orders depended on his working hours. Yue copied the start time onto his own tally before the crew borrowed the key. He put the tally where he could see it from the bench.

salt_channels_002.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_002.text: The level staff showed a fall toward the reed bank, though the newer plan marked the channel as uphill. Yue first turned the sheet upside down. The error stayed. A survey worker found that the copy had transposed the two datum marks. The mistake explained a bad drawing, not the sound beneath the pavement. Duan kept them as separate observations while the crew established a fresh level from the exposed spring wall.

salt_channels_003.speaker: duan_zhi
salt_channels_003.text: 'It is pleasant when a wrong page explains everything,' Duan said. 'Usually it explains the page.' He sent the mason to inspect the wall's exposed joints, then sat in the shade to compare the two staff readings. His injured leg limited the slope he could stand on safely. Yue moved the table closer so he could see both marks without climbing. He thanked her as plainly as he corrected her map.

salt_channels_004.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_004.text: The mason found a narrow wet seam beneath the approach, away from the drinking-water outlet. The crew placed an ordinary catch tray under the accessible drip. They timed the fill through three equal intervals while a second worker measured the inlet. Yue wanted the tray's steady stream to be their missing supply. The first sum was smaller than the hoped-for difference. She wrote it without rounding upward.

salt_channels_005.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_005.text: A little boy from a nearby house watched the catch tray and asked whether he could drink from it. Yue said the water had crossed old mortar and had not been tested for drinking. He complained that she was putting clean-looking water back in the ditch while his grandmother paid the cart. The complaint stayed with her after he ran home. A safe answer could still sound cruel when it described a shortage that remained.

salt_channels_006.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_006.text: At midday the crew delivered a notice about the catch water to nearby collectors. It could be used only for the specific nonfood cleaning tasks the clinician approved after inspection. Nobody had permission to improvise a new drinking point. Xiu's household team arranged essential jars for the grandmother through the corrected temporary rule. The little boy returned with his own cup and showed Yue that someone had already filled it.

salt_channels_007.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_007.text: Below the approach, a settling shutter rattled against its frame. The brine mantis behind it lifted its mineral combs when the crew's boots shook the plank. Duan stopped the workers on the dry side. The creature was defending the pool where salt fines had collected. Moving the shutter now would squeeze that pool toward the clean outlet. The crew widened the old settling exit with an ordinary hooked board while keeping the intake closed.

salt_channels_008.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_008.text: The mantis retreated along the sheltered exit, spraying a discarded strip connected to the isolated tester's measured reference stone. Salt bridged its exposed contacts. A false bright mark spent the tester's finite charge; Yue admitted no qi of her own. They disconnected the stone and covered the contaminated strip as waste. The miller had once been told a brighter conductor meant a stronger worker. He asked what to do with a similar strip in his cupboard.

salt_channels_009.speaker: lin_yue
salt_channels_009.text: 'Show the examiner before using it,' Yue said. 'Do not let this example certify yours either way.' The miller fetched the strip in its dry wrapping and Duan arranged a separate later inspection. Yue felt a small relief at giving an answer with a destination. The safe instruction did not require the man to understand every contact diagram before he could stop trusting a misleading light.

salt_channels_010.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_010.text: Once the settling exit was clear, the mason inspected the shutter seating from the dry access. An old repair had joined the clean overflow and waste flush through a common notch. At high lake levels the back pressure had hidden its loss. Now the lower lake drew a steady branch away. The mechanism belonged to changed water levels and an inadequate separation, not a creature's appetite for the households' supply.

salt_channels_011.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_011.text: The miller remembered who cut the notch but hesitated to name him. The man had died two winters earlier. His apprentice still repaired gates in the valley. Duan asked for the actual repair order rather than a story inherited with the tools. It authorized emergency flood relief under conditions that no longer held. Nobody had signed a dry-season reassessment. The apprentice's present skill did not make him responsible for his teacher's old instruction.

salt_channels_012.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_012.text: Yue copied the order at the miller's table. Its date matched a season when the boundary dispute had closed the lower road. She wondered whether fear of that road had kept workers from returning. The miller said he could not speak for all crews; his own mill stayed open until ice damaged the wheel. She crossed out the sentence she had begun about a whole frightened village and kept his narrower account.

salt_channels_013.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_013.text: After the noon meal, qualified masons fitted a removable divider at the common notch. Mechanical clamps and a rated shutter carried the present head; inspected seal packing did not rely on fresh mortar curing under load. Yue passed tools from a level board. There was no useful prepared qi task in carrying the tool pan. Her two arm pairs rested while her ordinary forearms tired. She changed with the next carrier before the pan began to tilt.

salt_channels_014.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_014.text: The first repeat brought the collection outlet to one hundred forty-seven jars per day on the measured interval. Duan treated that as raw flow, not drinking clearance. Level variation and collection loss suggested a conservative one hundred forty-five if the water passed inspection. A second worker retained the measurements. The extra flow had a visible channel source. It still needed safe separation, flushing and an independent quality check before anyone could count it toward essential supply.

salt_channels_015.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_015.text: At the far branch, two worn marker posts identified the reserve overflow's lower edge. A wet ribbon continued toward the reeds. Closing it completely might recover more water, but would also drain a pool where the Listener's nest reeds grew. Su Lan arrived to confirm that the channel crew's permit stopped at the marker. They could measure public flow there. Altering the far habitat required another proposal and the people who tended it.

salt_channels_016.speaker: su_lan
salt_channels_016.text: 'The Listener helped keep living households safe,' she said. 'That gives it a place in the conversation. It does not make every reed its private property, or every useful pool ours to empty.' The miller wanted a clean ownership answer. Su Lan offered the current permit instead. The near repair could proceed without settling the whole bank. He accepted that smaller answer because his wheel could work under it.

salt_channels_017.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_017.text: On the second morning, the crew repeated the yield measurement with the mill race operating. The independent water inspector checked separation, flushed the repaired outlet, and compared recovered water with the approved spring source for contamination under the village's drinking criteria. The initial flush was discarded. Only after clearance did Duan approve the conservative usable yield. The report retained the checks and gate settings. The miller could resume flour work without relying on Yue's reassurance.

salt_channels_018.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_018.text: Yue checked the exposed low bank for a safe walking approach. A hollow beneath one board had widened during the lowered-water period. The board was closed to foot traffic until its ordinary support could be replaced. She wanted to step across it as neatly as she had learned at the sluice, then saw that a prepared movement would only hide the missing ground for one person. She tied the warning cord instead.

salt_channels_019.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_019.text: Before leaving, Duan asked her to state the result without saying that they had solved the shortage. Yue described the common-notch loss, the removable divider, the repeated conservative yield and the unopened far-bank question. The supply would still fall five counted jars short of daily essentials. Industrial and seed uses would draw the reserve. Duan made her put that sentence first, where a celebration could not bury it.

salt_channels_020.speaker: narrator
salt_channels_020.text: The crew returned the miller's key and added his lost hours to the commission's shutdown tally. The grain-house steward collected a flour order delayed by the inspection and complained that the seed team would now work late. Neither person praised the report. Yue carried it back anyway. Under the report's exact water claim were the hands that had kept the mill still, fed the crew and waited for work to begin again.

salt_accounts_001.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_001.text: An Ru brought Yue to the salt merchant's store, where raised planks kept purchase books above the damp floor. The merchant set three of his own dispatch volumes on the counter. Household customers could permit copies of their individual bills later. The public reserve invoices were already open under the council's contract. An Ru asked for those first. A large open stack could look like cooperation while still wasting their paid inspection hours.

salt_accounts_002.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_002.text: The first dispatch invoice charged for twelve water jars and a freight journey. Its total was higher than twelve times the advertised jar price. Yue recognized the ordinary household concern: had a high payment bought less water than expected? The separate carriage charge explained the sum on this invoice. It did not explain why the customer had been told that the whole sum purchased water. The merchant admitted his counter board did not show the distinction.

salt_accounts_003.speaker: an_ru
salt_accounts_003.text: 'We can require a clearer bill without calling the journey imaginary,' An Ru said. 'This driver carried the load. We have his road tally and the receiving marks. The disputed household's standing survives whichever line caused its overpayment.' Yue kept the dispatch evidence beneath the freight column. She had hoped for a thief simple enough to accuse with one sum. The actual work had more columns and fewer satisfying entrances.

salt_accounts_004.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_004.text: The merchant consented to a corrected public price board. It listed water, ordinary carriage, jar deposit and deposit return separately. He objected when Yue wanted the board read aloud at the collection point; he thought that would sound like a confession. An Ru offered to read the new terms without claiming that every old sale had been wrongful. The objection changed into a request that he stand beside her and answer questions.

salt_accounts_005.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_005.text: A reserve invoice named twenty-one jars for absent-household holding. The corresponding dispatch line sent those jars to the cooperative's salt wash. Yue checked the date against the restored land notice. The sale came afterward. A second invoice repeated the same quantity a week later; two more made eighty-four jars. The water had moved. Their first useful finding was that the supposedly held supply could not still be sitting in a hidden tank.

salt_accounts_006.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_006.text: The cooperative steward arrived with the actual receiving book. He had bought a permitted industrial batch at the reserve's sale price. His workers used it to finish an old wash order. He had not been told that the council's water account charged the batch against nineteen household credits. Yue could see the two transaction descriptions without deciding whether the steward had known the concealed one. An Ru requested the authorizing order.

salt_accounts_007.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_007.text: The allocation supervisor's signed order called the commercial payment a temporary substitute for household delivery. Its public summary claimed the absent households had failed to collect. Those households were present in the corrected land register, and the temporary collection point had never notified them of a turn. The supervisor said the water would have spoiled if left standing. Duan's cistern maintenance rule allowed storage for much longer than the interval on the invoices.

salt_accounts_008.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_008.text: An Ru let the supervisor read the comparison without the merchant standing over him. He admitted signing the order and disputed the description of it as concealment. Salt wages, he said, had kept families fed while the water matter waited. Yue asked which families had been consulted about exchanging their water credits for that wage protection. He could name the cooperative board. None represented the nineteen households charged in the absent column.

salt_accounts_009.speaker: lin_yue
salt_accounts_009.text: 'The wage need can be real,' Yue said. 'It still does not let that board spend somebody else's credit without asking.' She felt the sentence sharpen in her mouth and checked the invoice dates again before going further. Four signed payments supported this particular comparison. They did not tell her how every salt contract had been approved, or which other household accounts might contain the same defect.

salt_accounts_010.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_010.text: The receiving cashier opened the commercial proceeds page. After eight copper of documented carriage, eighty-four copper remained in a sealed council purse. It was earmarked for the same absent-household column, but no disbursement had been posted. The cashier counted it before two witnesses, then sealed it again. An Ru recorded both sums. Finding the money did not put eighty-four water jars back into the cistern.

salt_accounts_011.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_011.text: The water clerk had copied the absent column from the older turn book. He showed a correction slip that he had prepared after the land hearing and never sent to the allocation supervisor. The supervisor said he had received no such slip. A receiving register contained no entry for it. The unused correction could explain the clerk's knowledge and delay. It could not prove a delivery that the dispatch books placed elsewhere.

salt_accounts_012.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_012.text: Yue wanted to ask why nobody had chased the slip. An Ru asked first who had been responsible for the handoff. The clerk's appointment named one receiving office and a monthly check, both of which existed. His private worry about making a mistake did not erase the duty. The report retained his offered explanation without turning it into a defense the affected households would have to accept.

salt_accounts_013.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_013.text: At lunch, the merchant complained that the new board would drive customers to a rival cart. The rival charged a smaller advertised price but kept deposits after broken jars. Yue could not settle that business by comparing two slogans. She suggested showing the return condition on his own board. He ate in silence, then asked his son to bring a sample jar so people could see which cracks disqualified a return.

salt_accounts_014.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_014.text: The son was already doing deliveries and wanted his wages raised for the new counter work. The merchant began to say that learning the family trade was enough reward. An Ru waited while the young man listed his actual additional hours. Their exchange did not belong in the reserve fraud finding. Yue left it out of the report, and noticed that leaving it out did not require pretending she had not heard him.

salt_accounts_015.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_015.text: On the second morning, the household team brought permission for two water-credit comparisons. The owners approved quantities and dated collection attempts, with their unrelated debts covered. Both had asked for water while their turns were still marked absent. Their receipts bore the collection clerk's refusal mark. The evidence established those requests. The other seventeen households would not need to reveal debts to keep their already restored standing.

salt_accounts_016.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_016.text: The supervisor returned with a proposed repayment schedule that would spread the eighty-four copper over six months. An Ru pointed to the counted purse on the table. It was already council money received from the disputed sale. No installment schedule was needed to return that existing balance. His proposal concerned additional penalties and interest that the audit had not yet established. Yue kept those demands off the immediate refund order.

salt_accounts_017.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_017.text: Before returning the books, they copied the public invoice numbers and quantities into a comparison sheet signed by the merchant and cashier. The receiving cooperative retained its own originals. An Ru sealed the supervisor's submitted order and offered him a receipt. The copy room would hold the public packet. Private household slips would go back to their owners unless they separately chose a longer deposit for further review.

salt_accounts_018.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_018.text: The keeper checked the page binding while Yue counted the eighty-four copper again with the cashier. A copper fell into a floor crack. For a foolish instant, Yue thought losing that one coin would undo the whole discovery. The merchant's son lifted the loose plank with an ordinary wedge. They found the coin beside a dried bean, put each in its proper place, and completed the count.

salt_accounts_019.speaker: an_ru
salt_accounts_019.text: 'Our report asks for the present turn book corrected, eighty-four copper restored to the water-credit purse, and review of the four signed diversions,' An Ru said. 'It does not announce that eighty-four jars will arrive tomorrow. It does not determine every officer's sanction. Those questions have their own receiving dates.' Yue copied the dates before the conclusion. A refund without a place to claim it could become another absent column.

salt_accounts_020.speaker: narrator
salt_accounts_020.text: At the square, the corrected price board stood beside the restored names. The merchant was answering a question about returning an intact jar. Yue carried a thinner packet than the stack she had first wanted to inspect. Its essential comparison survived without borrowed outrage from unrelated accounts. Across the room, Duan's crew had chalk on their sleeves and Xiu's team had a map of collection walks. The audit needed their findings before it could describe the shortage.

salt_households_001.speaker: narrator
salt_households_001.text: Wei Xiu began at the collection point rather than the archive. Five women and two men waited with empty jars, each keeping a place for someone working an early shift. Xiu explained the paid listening task and offered to come back later to anyone who preferred privacy. Two declined. Their jars joined the essential turn anyway. Yue watched the line advance without making consent to her questions another queue.

salt_households_002.speaker: narrator
salt_households_002.text: The first collector wanted to show the walk before showing a bill. Her north-bank home stood beyond a steep stair that flooded during high lake water and crumbled now that the bank was dry. She could carry one full ten-litre jar safely. Her household's daily allowance needed three. The water entitlement on a board did not include the extra journeys in her legs. Xiu timed the climb at the woman's ordinary pace.

salt_households_003.speaker: narrator
salt_households_003.text: Yue offered to carry a second jar and was told that a visitor's strong day would not solve a month. She put it down. The woman then accepted help on that particular trip, making the difference herself. At the door they set both jars on a low shelf. A child asked whether Yue had come to return their name again. Xiu answered that nobody needed to surrender it for this visit.

salt_households_004.speaker: wei_xiu
salt_households_004.text: 'A collection point can be open and still be difficult to reach,' Xiu said when they returned. 'The north route needs a nearer ordinary shelf and a paid carrier turn. I can help plan the landing approach. I cannot promise my ferry crew will carry a week's water for free.' Yue drew the possible shelf on the map. She had wanted to offer generosity. Xiu was asking for something that would remain after generosity went home.

salt_households_005.speaker: narrator
salt_households_005.text: A second household permitted inspection of two refusal slips. Each bore a clerk's mark under the absent heading, dated after the land record correction. The owner kept his private debt booklet shut. Yue copied the quantities and collection dates he approved, then asked whether he wanted his name attached to the public report. He chose a household code. Xiu retained the code key with the owner instead of handing it to the council.

salt_households_006.speaker: narrator
salt_households_006.text: The owner worked at the salt wash. His wages depended on the very industrial water now paused while his drinking turn was corrected. Yue nearly asked which need mattered more to him. He answered before she did: the village should not require him to pick between his child drinking and his own shift being paid. He could support a water limit while asking the cooperative to negotiate honest short-work wages.

salt_households_007.speaker: narrator
salt_households_007.text: At the next door, a woman said she had collected her full drinking turn throughout the dispute by borrowing her sister's registered place. The practice had left her sister's jars short, so the two households purchased extra cart water together. Restoring the names did not erase that private arrangement. She wanted a separate collection token now. She did not want the council to publish how often her sister had gone without washing.

salt_households_008.speaker: narrator
salt_households_008.text: Xiu explained that the temporary essential rule already allowed the separate token. They went to the clerk together and received it without filing the private story. Yue wrote the completed practical correction in the public report. Later, in her own notebook, she left a blank where the hidden washing details might have made her prose more moving. The family's permission was not a challenge to write a better disguise.

salt_households_009.speaker: narrator
salt_households_009.text: They ate bread on the landing's high side while Wei Jin unloaded ordinary jar carriers. Some straps cut too sharply into shoulders. A potter offered felt pads left from another job; the repair still needed stitching time. Xiu priced two paid sewing shifts rather than asking the potter's daughter to fit every pad after work. The daughter inspected the sample strap, named her rate and made one demonstration while the group ate.

salt_households_010.speaker: narrator
salt_households_010.text: Ren Qiao, visiting from the orchard under paid clinic coverage, met them at the valley delivery shelf. The orchard matron retained her own schedule. During the present drought, this valley clinic had separately paused its local exchange booth. Its essential claim covered drinking, ordinary wound cleaning and food preparation, with safe handwashing storage. Ren showed quantities and patient count while keeping treatment records private. Nobody's injury would become public proof just to defend the clinic's turn.

salt_households_011.speaker: ren_qiao
salt_households_011.text: 'A frightened council sometimes asks the sick to display suffering before it believes a number,' he said. 'I can certify the treatment quantities and answer a qualified reviewer. I will not bring patients to the square as measuring jars.' Yue looked at the doorway wide enough for a carried bed. She remembered how much easier a promise sounded when the person paying for it was absent from the room.

salt_households_012.speaker: narrator
salt_households_012.text: On the reed-bank path, the Listener waited beside a nest it had woven for itself. No household tablet was being collected for a new shelter bargain. Xiu asked whether the channel's low flow affected the reed beds. The Listener described the shallow pools it had watched through the last five days. It had not watched the spring head or measured the drinking outlet. Yue recorded the duration beside the report.

salt_households_013.speaker: reed_listener
salt_households_013.text: 'When the first pool dried, the small ones walked over mud to the second,' the Listener said. 'I saw tracks. I cannot tell you which will survive another dry week.' Its wet-slate feathers trembled in the breeze. Yue could ask it to observe one marked pool if it chose, with another person checking the visible level. She could not make its old protection of names a debt requiring a permanent watch.

salt_households_014.speaker: narrator
salt_households_014.text: The Listener agreed to leave an ordinary reed mark at the visible pool edge each afternoon for three days. A shore worker would compare the marks from the public path. The agreement needed no name surrender, fuel drawing or private memory. Xiu left the farther reed bank out of their access map. It could enter a future habitat proposal if the people who tended it wished to join that work.

salt_households_015.speaker: narrator
salt_households_015.text: At dusk, a salt worker invited them to a supper where the paused shifts had become the main conversation. He said that returned rights had made the council less afraid to ignore inconvenient people, because it thought its old wrong was settled. His sister disagreed. The collection token had changed her week. Yue let both sentences stand in the listening notes. A single conclusion about how everyone felt would have lost one of them.

salt_households_016.speaker: narrator
salt_households_016.text: The next morning they followed an early carrier round. The work began before the square's bell because children needed porridge before school. A public time signal at midday would not schedule that need. Su Lan offered an ordinary posted dawn marker and a paid bell turn if the council funded it. The listening team's map separated collection times from announcements so the tower would not claim that sounding once supplied every doorstep.

salt_households_017.speaker: narrator
salt_households_017.text: A wheel came loose on the second carrier cart near the high-bank turn. The loaded jars remained strapped, but the driver could not bring them down safely. Xiu stopped the next cart above him. Yue helped unload from the checked level side, with no reinforcement on the suspect wheel. A repair worker replaced the peg. The incident added a spare-wheel cost to the delivery proposal and no dramatic technique to Yue's examination record.

salt_households_018.speaker: narrator
salt_households_018.text: The family waiting below missed its usual breakfast time. Their essential water was still theirs; the delay did not become refusal or absence in the turn book. The carrier gave a dated late-delivery slip and the clinic moved its delivery by half an hour to make room. An ordinary scheduling correction had prevented a damaged wheel from becoming another false household entry. Yue copied the procedure while the family finally filled its cooking pot.

salt_households_019.speaker: narrator
salt_households_019.text: Before the shared meeting, Xiu laid the public route map beside the two approved refusal-slip copies. The north-bank collection shelf, carrier rate, dawn need and corrected tokens each had a current owner or duty. Private debt and illness stayed outside. Their map did not settle the industrial wage question. It showed why counting jars at one central tap had been too narrow a description of access.

salt_households_020.speaker: narrator
salt_households_020.text: Yue watched the last household collect without waiting for the team's report. She had once imagined help as a decisive arrival with the right question. Today it was a shelf, a spare peg, a collector allowed to decline, and a number that still had to fit the spring's supply. Xiu folded the map along its existing creases. They took it to the council without calling those modest repairs a complete return.

salt_findings_001.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_001.text: On the second evening, the council gathered at the watermill's shaded porch. Each team put its public report on a different mat. The reserve keeper counted sixteen hundred forty jars at the inspection's beginning and a conservative fifteen hundred eighty now. Two days of essential demand above the old spring yield had used sixty. Late recovered flow was not credited to that count. The new schedule would begin from the checked lower total the next morning.

salt_findings_002.speaker: duan_zhi
salt_findings_002.text: 'A common notch sent clean spring flow into the waste branch under the lake's present low head,' Duan reported. 'Qualified masons separated it with a removable divider and repeated the check with the mill operating. We count one hundred forty-five jars a day provisionally. That still leaves five to draw daily for essentials. The farther reed bank remains outside this repair permit. Neither a bright contact nor a drained habitat supplied our gain.'

salt_findings_003.speaker: yuan_lian
salt_findings_003.text: 'I am Yuan Lian, forewoman of this mill,' the woman beside the wheel said. 'I signed the second operating check and will post the noon flow count. The miller's lost grinding hours are on the shutdown account; my workers will receive their ordinary wages. If the counted yield drops, optional turns stop first. A clerk will have to tell the cooperative that plainly instead of asking my crew to hide the shortfall in a nicer number.'

salt_findings_004.speaker: an_ru
salt_findings_004.text: 'Four signed orders diverted eighty-four reserve jars from the absent-household credit to commercial salt wash after the restored land notice,' An Ru said. 'The receiving books establish delivery. The sale's eighty-four copper net remains in a counted council purse after eight copper carriage. Return that balance to the household water-credit account. It is money, not water still stored. Responsibility for the signed diversions will receive its own hearing and reply date.'

salt_findings_005.speaker: wei_xiu
salt_findings_005.text: 'Two approved refusal slips show collection attempts recorded as absence,' Xiu reported. 'The temporary essential rule has corrected those turns. The north-bank route also needs a closer shelf, a paid carrier and a spare cart peg. Families can decline interviews and still collect. Clinic demand is certified through treatment quantities, not patient display. A central tap's open gate did not tell the whole story of who could carry water home.'

salt_findings_006.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_006.text: The allocation supervisor stood to answer before the council accepted the reports. He said that the salt orders had protected wages, and that he had treated the commercial payment as a future household benefit. An Ru placed the approval signatures beside the missing notices. The council found that the nineteen households had never accepted that exchange. It corrected the current turn book immediately and recorded the supervisor's disputed explanation for the later responsibility hearing.

salt_findings_007.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_007.text: The cashier transferred the counted eighty-four copper to the corrected water-credit purse under two receiving signatures. Household claims would be calculated from the four invoiced diversions, with a public receipt route and private balance reviews. The refund was not made conditional on agreeing with the next allocation plan. Yue watched one recipient ask to take her balance later because she was going directly to work. The cashier gave her a dated claim slip.

salt_findings_008.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_008.text: On the porch, the salt cooperative asked whether the correction meant industrial use would remain shut all season. Yuan Lian pointed to the counted reserve above the thousand-jar floor. It was real water, available for a limited trial if the council accepted the draw. She wanted the trial's ordinary handling hours paid even when a batch failed. The cooperative could discuss its price loss without making the forewoman's workers absorb that loss invisibly.

salt_findings_009.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_009.text: The grain-house steward brought three trays, each holding a different seed lot. One lot needed an approved clean-water rinse before drying; another could be sorted dry; the third was already too moulded to distribute safely. He opposed a trial that poured the same amount onto every tray for the sake of equal treatment. A seed sample could narrow the request. It could not create a harvest guarantee to trade against thirsty households.

salt_findings_010.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_010.text: The near-term calculation used twenty-one days from the repaired supply's first morning, with no promised rainfall counted. Essential demand above the conservative spring yield would draw one hundred five reserve jars. A first three-day trial could use at most ninety additional jars. Later optional work could use at most three hundred forty. Even that combined maximum left at least one thousand forty-five counted jars, including forty-five of contingency above the protected floor.

salt_findings_011.speaker: lin_yue
salt_findings_011.text: 'The forty-five are not a prize for whoever asks last,' Yue said. 'They cover a changed flow, transfer loss beyond the counted allowance, or a new essential need before the review.' Duan asked her what happened if those needs exceeded forty-five. She answered that optional work stopped and the council met again. The written ceiling was a way to notice the limit early, not permission to keep drawing until a paper promise came true.

salt_findings_012.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_012.text: Ren Qiao set an orchard appointment page beside the water plan. The paced-breathing proposal had required Yue's personal return after a month; if that was the accepted arrangement, its visit was now overdue. The other proposals assigned different duties. They checked the agreement actually retained, preserving its owners and dates. Foundry study and storm work could not secretly fulfill an orchard visit. Yue found the comparison uncomfortable precisely because no ingenious channel repair could answer it.

salt_findings_013.speaker: ren_qiao
salt_findings_013.text: 'I can receive a permitted update and speak with the matron about a new date for any visit you still owe,' Ren said. 'That update does not become the visit. The orchard will decide whether the new date works.' Yue offered the commission's paid rest afternoon for writing and asked the carrier for the actual journey fare. She would not promise a return between two shifts until someone had shown her a route she could take.

salt_findings_014.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_014.text: Yuan Lian turned the mill's ordinary clock so its face could be read from the porch. The three-day trial needed daylight checks and fixed delivery hours, not a new binding command. Su Lan offered the tower's tested time circuit for public announcements, using whatever equipment the tower's own keeper had accepted. The circuit would not decide household standing, close a disputed gate or grant a stranger authority over the reed bank.

salt_findings_015.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_015.text: Each trial proposal named a different immediate cost. Ninety optional jars could test reduced salt washing and help keep the nine-day order alive. Thirty could test the threatened seed lot and leave more reserve. Using none could test the essential delivery route and obtain a stronger loss account before granting industrial water. All three had paid workers and independently continuing tasks elsewhere. Choosing one would place the first scarce optional turn somewhere concrete.

salt_findings_016.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_016.text: Before the decision, the council authorized the separate shelf and carrier work under its access fund. The eighty-four copper refund stayed outside that budget. Yuan Lian signed for the noon flow count; the reserve keeper signed the morning measure; the council chair named the person who would receive a stop notice. Yue read the three names aloud. Somebody had to own the ordinary action that followed an alarming number.

salt_findings_017.speaker: narrator
salt_findings_017.text: The porch emptied briefly for supper. Wei Xiu filled a cup for Yue and asked whether she planned to stay beyond the commission. Yue said she had not decided. The answer did not wound Xiu as Yue feared. 'Then decide before I sell customers a place on your boat,' the pilot said. Her humor carried a serious boundary: affection could welcome a person, but an allocation schedule needed actual accepted hours.

salt_trial_choice.speaker: lin_yue
salt_trial_choice.text: The first optional allowance could support only one supervised three-day experiment. Essential supply, corrected turns and paid access work would proceed whichever experiment Yue joined. She could test whether ninety jars protected a reduced salt order, use thirty on the threatened seed lot, or draw no optional water while improving the essential carrier route. The later council would hear the chosen trial's result before adopting a longer allocation.

choices.text: Use ninety optional jars to test reduced salt washing.
Use thirty optional jars to test the threatened seed lot.
Use no optional jars; test essential delivery and reserve accounting.

salt_water_clearance.speaker: narrator
salt_water_clearance.text: The independent water inspector supplied the clearance record. The repaired clean branch had been isolated from the waste pool, flushed, and tested against the approved spring source for the village's drinking criteria. Initial flush water was discarded during the second inspection day; none counted as recovered household supply. The daily one hundred forty-five was the conservative usable rate after clearance. A failed repeat would close that outlet and trigger the lower-yield emergency review.

salt_wash_trial_001.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_001.text: The salt trial began with thirty counted jars in an isolated working tank. Yuan Lian locked its feed after the reserve keeper entered the draw. Household water stayed on the essential branch. The cooperative foreman had wanted the full sixty-jar washing turn he knew; the trial would give half that daily amount for three days. His workers laid out three smaller batches, refusing to promise the old output from the new allowance.

salt_wash_trial_002.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_002.text: Yue washed a marked sack beside a worker who had done the job for twelve years. The worker watched the grit settling through cloth and stopped her from reusing a final rinse as if it were clean input. Spent water could serve approved first-stage industrial washing elsewhere, with separate tanks and quality checks. It could not return to drinking storage. The worker said this distinction slowly, because clever visitors usually heard only the word reuse.

salt_wash_trial_003.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_003.text: A prepared dosing gate had stuck during its dry test. Duan replaced the worn stop before permitting use. Yue could give its rated control socket a quarter-unit command through her first pair, spending the known half-unit including delivery loss; ordinary gravity moved the water. She discharged fully and let the foreman measure the tank's actual draw. The faint control light certified no salt purity and supplied none of the washing volume.

salt_wash_trial_004.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_004.text: By the end of the first day, two sacks met the buyer's reduced-rinse grade and one failed it. The rejected sack went into the raw-salt bin with its test mark intact. The foreman wanted to scrape the mark off before the merchant saw it. Yuan Lian refused; reclassifying a failed sample was part of the trial, concealing it was not. He agreed after the cooperative board guaranteed the workers' trial wages.

salt_wash_trial_005.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_005.text: At supper, the foreman told Yue that he had once paid a cart fee from his own pocket rather than send his crew home unpaid. She believed him and still remembered his hand over the failed mark. A person could protect workers in one moment and make them vulnerable in another. She did not offer forgiveness he had not asked for. She asked whether tomorrow's rejected sacks had a receiving bin and an agreed price.

salt_wash_trial_006.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_006.text: The buyer inspected the marked samples on the second morning. Reduced-rinse salt fetched less than the original refined order, but more than unwashed raw salt. She offered an amended contract for qualifying sacks and a separate raw purchase. The cooperative could refuse the amendment. It could not truthfully deliver the reduced batch under the earlier refined label. The board spent an hour arguing while the paid trial crew repaired a drying rack.

salt_wash_trial_007.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_007.text: On the third day, a settling cloth tore and spoiled one of the permitted batches. Yuan Lian stopped the dosing gate rather than borrowing an extra household jar to wash away the mistake. The board signed the batch loss. Yue helped fit a sound spare cloth, then cleaned the failed sack's mark without erasing its classification. The allowance remained thirty jars. A practical repair did not buy another water turn.

salt_wash_trial_008.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_008.text: The three days spent ninety optional jars and fifteen for the gap between essential demand and the repaired spring supply. From fifteen hundred eighty, the reserve's conservative count stood at fourteen hundred seventy-five. The lost batch had used part of the ninety; it was not quietly reimbursed with a ninety-first jar. The cashier entered its wage loss separately from the water ledger. Yuan Lian made both books available to the council.

salt_wash_trial_009.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_009.text: At the receiving table, the cooperative approved the amended grade contract and a smaller shipping volume. The price loss remained. Workers received the guaranteed trial wage and learned the board's proposed rate for future smaller shifts. Some accepted it; others asked to take grain-house or carrier work instead. Yue's report described those decisions without calling every person grateful for a shortage handled honestly.

salt_wash_trial_010.speaker: narrator
salt_wash_trial_010.text: She returned with sample grades, the actual ninety-jar draw and a contract that could keep part of the nine-day order alive. It proved the reduced washing plan possible under its tested conditions. It did not prove that every sack could be saved or that the seed lot needed no water. The first optional turn had carried a real choice into people's wages; the next meeting would have to look at that consequence directly.

salt_seed_trial_001.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_001.text: The grain-house trial received ten counted jars on its first morning. The steward placed the threatened seed lot beside two dry-sorted controls, keeping labels on all three. Yue wanted the water to save the lot that looked saddest. The steward asked her to look at the sample test instead. Seeds too damaged for safe planting would be rejected even if their owners had the strongest need for a harvest.

salt_seed_trial_002.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_002.text: The potter supplied shallow drying trays under a separate paid order. Zhen, passing through with ceramic repairs, checked their glaze and found one rough lip likely to hold dirty rinse residue. The tray went back for replacement. His second-stage field had no part in the inspection. He ran a cloth along the lip and let Yue feel the snag. The work was careful enough to matter without needing a higher realm.

salt_seed_trial_003.speaker: zhen
salt_seed_trial_003.text: 'People pay more attention when I say a glaze interferes with a formation,' Zhen said. 'They should also listen when it traps dirt.' He set the rejected tray apart. Yue laughed, then asked whether he wanted to join the commission after his delivery. He had a kiln shift already accepted at home. He could inspect this paid order today without letting their friendship overwrite tomorrow's work.

salt_seed_trial_004.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_004.text: The approved rinse used the day's ten jars, then drained into a labelled industrial waste tank. The wet seeds needed air and shade rather than another pour. When an impatient helper suggested qi heat, the steward pointed to the temperature limit. Yue had no tested seed-drying technique. They opened an ordinary shutter and moved the trays to the checked draft, leaving the faster idea unwritten as an available treatment.

salt_seed_trial_005.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_005.text: Two dry control samples passed the qualified inspector's viability comparison more reliably than the rinsed lot. The result embarrassed the steward because he had argued so loudly for clean water. He reread the labels before reporting it. This lot's damage had already exceeded what the approved wash could remove. The grain house could protect the healthier dry-sorted seed instead of spending more water to defend his first request.

salt_seed_trial_006.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_006.text: The second day tested a smaller salvage fraction under the same total ten-jar allowance. A neighboring farmer offered to take the rejected grain for animals. The steward asked the qualified seed inspector whether that use was safe; mould could harm livestock too. The answer ruled it out for the tested fraction. A poor crop did not become useful feed merely because another household was willing to bear the unseen risk.

salt_seed_trial_007.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_007.text: On the third morning, the salvage fraction passed its limited planting test. It was small enough to mark for a separate bed rather than mix through the general seed issue. Yue helped count packets while another worker verified the labels. The farmer who had offered livestock use returned to ask about wages for the trial garden. The grain house offered a paid short contract, with the uncertain yield written plainly.

salt_seed_trial_008.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_008.text: The trial spent thirty optional jars and fifteen for the repaired supply's essential shortfall. The conservative reserve count stood at fifteen hundred thirty-five from the same fifteen hundred eighty starting balance. No predicted harvest entered that water balance. The steward retained rejected samples for the announced review period under approved disposal conditions. Their unpleasant smell reminded Yue that a successful salvage packet did not erase the much larger failed lot.

salt_seed_trial_009.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_009.text: The salt cooperative's foreman came to the grain house to ask whether his crew's paused shifts had saved anything. The steward showed him the small salvage fraction and the healthier dry controls. He did not hide how little the water had rescued. The foreman was angry about the waiting order. They arranged a council discussion of alternate work and raw-salt freight rather than trying to buy his approval with an inflated seed claim.

salt_seed_trial_010.speaker: narrator
salt_seed_trial_010.text: Yue carried the limited planting result, the thirty-jar draw and the updated seed request back to the council. The chosen trial had preserved some seed while showing that the original water demand was too broad. It had left the salt order to other negotiations for three days. She could describe both consequences without turning them into a contest about which worker cared more for the valley's future.

salt_reserve_trial_001.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_001.text: The reserve trial began without an optional water draw. Xiu and Yue joined the essential carrier route while Yuan Lian supervised the independent spring checks. The cooperative's washing tank stayed shut; the grain steward continued dry sorting. Nobody had been promised that those pauses were painless. The commission paid its carrier hours and required the other teams to bring actual delay costs to the next meeting.

salt_reserve_trial_002.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_002.text: At dawn, Xiu found three collection tokens assigned to the same household. One was its newly issued token, another was the sister's older borrowed place, and the third had been copied from a temporary slip. The family was entitled to its full essential quantity once. The clerk cancelled the duplicate instruments under the owner's explanation without cancelling the household's restored standing. Yue wondered how many shortages had been made harder to see by confusing tokens with people.

salt_reserve_trial_003.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_003.text: The north-bank shelf stood closer to the steep houses, but its lowest plank sagged under a full jar. The carpenter propped it for the current load and named the cost of a permanent replacement. The temporary work was marked with a safe maximum. Xiu did not announce the shelf complete because its paint was dry. A collector could read the load mark without knowing which council officer had promised the improved route.

salt_reserve_trial_004.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_004.text: On the second round, Yue carried an empty practice jar through the tight turn while Xiu watched her ordinary footing. A prepared reinforced step could make one movement smoother; this route required repeatable work through an entire shift. They widened the turn by moving a loose fence panel with its owner's permission. The change cost no qi and required no claim that the path had become universally safe for every cart.

salt_reserve_trial_005.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_005.text: The reserve keeper used a sealed measure from the turn book's calibration. His older delivery scoop held less than its painted line implied. They corrected the scoop and retained its old marking in the inspection note. Current essential portions still totalled one hundred fifty counted jars daily. Documented earlier short portions received claim slips for a separately authorized settlement review, with no extra trial draw. Historical claims and today's physical water count stayed in different columns.

salt_reserve_trial_006.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_006.text: A carrier complained that the corrections would lengthen his route after the paid hours ended. Xiu paused the round and asked the council's receiving officer for a revised shift. The officer approved a paid replacement for the final stair deliveries. Yue had expected a refusal and had started to plan doing them herself after supper. She crossed that plan out when the replacement accepted. Planning paid work had made an ordinary institutional answer possible.

salt_reserve_trial_007.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_007.text: At the mill, Yuan Lian showed them two flow readings below the day's earlier rate. The conservative daily total still met one hundred forty-five after its counted allowance. She kept the lower readings on the public board instead of displaying only the best interval. The cooperative's foreman accused her of making the shortage look worse. She invited him to witness the next measure, then ended the discussion when her crew's meal break began.

salt_reserve_trial_008.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_008.text: The trial drew fifteen reserve jars for the essential shortfall and no optional jars. The conservative balance stood at fifteen hundred sixty-five. The old eighty-four-jar commercial diversion was already reflected in the physical starting count; it was not subtracted a second time. The eighty-four copper refund remained a separate money balance. Yue wrote those distinctions beside the totals after a council member tried to add the refund to stored water.

salt_reserve_trial_009.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_009.text: On the third evening, the carrier team had a load-marked shelf, corrected tokens, a calibrated scoop and a paid replacement procedure. The salt foreman had a list of delayed wash batches; the steward had dry seed sorting results and an unresolved rinse request. Preserving the reserve had purchased more time to choose. It had also spent three days that those other workers could not recover from a jar total.

salt_reserve_trial_010.speaker: narrator
salt_reserve_trial_010.text: Yue brought the conservative balance and the access changes to the shared meeting. The route worked better than it had at the trial's start. It had not made industrial work unnecessary, and it did not let the council promise that later water would arrive free of cost. Xiu set a worn carrier strap beside the report. Its new felt pad was an argument for continued paid attention, as concrete as any reserve number.

salt_grain_invoice.speaker: an_ru
salt_grain_invoice.text: The grain house has offered its rate sheet and a permitted comparison bill. A seasonal washing-water surcharge persisted on a dry-sorted lot with zero washing draw. The steward acknowledges that copied rate and withdraws it from such lots. Customers may submit their own bills for credit; no private account is opened automatically. This corrects the grain charge separately from the eighty-four-jar diversion. Neither refund adds water to our current physical count.

salt_recovery_001.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_001.text: On the evening after the three-day experiment, the chosen trial's signed report lay uppermost. Other crews brought only the work they had actually been permitted: dry sorting, source checks, carrier repairs and contract talks. Nobody invented an unchosen water test to make the packets equal. The reserve keeper copied the actual trial draw beside its starting count. The shared plan retained the ninety-jar ceiling as a conservative worst case, not a claim that all routes had spent it.

salt_recovery_002.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_002.text: Ren Qiao received Yue's permitted orchard update at the meeting's edge. They checked the appointment from her accepted arrangement and left any unfulfilled personal visit marked unfulfilled. A carrier would take the request for an agreed new date to the matron; until the reply came, it was a request. Yue wrote the journey fare beside it. A promise could become overdue without becoming worthless, but it needed an honest record and an answer from the person waiting.

salt_recovery_003.speaker: yuan_lian
salt_recovery_003.text: 'You can stay to read the noon count with me,' Yuan Lian offered. 'I have eighteen later days on this commission, then one closure day. I will not turn that into a season because people like having you at the porch.' Yue appreciated the blunt limit. The forewoman wanted a worker she could schedule, not a visitor's devotion measured by how difficult departure became.

salt_recovery_004.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_004.text: At the reed-bank marker, the shore worker compared the Listener's three offered marks with his own visible pool readings. Their reports agreed on a declining edge. The Listener chose not to extend its watch. The worker accepted the end date and prepared an ordinary future inspection under his own duties. Xiu kept the far-bank permit closed. A living habitat could enter their plan without becoming an unlimited witness for every water dispute.

salt_recovery_005.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_005.text: A Reedglass Salamander crouched beside the second pool, jade skin darkened by mud and mineral fronds along its back. It was about the size of a dog. When Yue's boot struck a loose stone, it moved under a reed shelf rather than toward her hand. She stepped back. Its visible shelter use supported keeping that shelf out of the near repair. It revealed no private history, measured no hidden spring and offered nobody an obligation to rescue it.

salt_recovery_006.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_006.text: On the return path, Yue found Xiu fitting a felt pad to a paid carrier's strap. The pilot asked which part of the trial she would remember first. Yue named its most difficult conversation. Xiu named the unbroken jar that reached a family's low shelf on time. Neither had the whole answer. They walked back together, with a spare cart peg knocking against the pilot's tool pouch.

salt_recovery_007.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_007.text: The cooperative had negotiated a reduced-grade or raw-salt receiving option, depending on actual later test results. The buyer would not certify an untested sack. The grain house reduced its demand to the lots that could justify washing, preserving dry sorting for the rest. Their revised requests made a smaller schedule possible. They did not erase wages already lost during the inspection and trial. The council retained those losses in the compensation review.

salt_recovery_008.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_008.text: The forewoman presented three eighteen-day proposals, each ending in the same twenty-one-day water review from the repair's first morning. A common rotation could grant up to two hundred seventy later wash jars and seventy seed jars. A reserve-first plan granted no later optional draw and paid eight temporary maintenance shifts from a separately voted access fund. A limited purchase plan granted at most two hundred later optional jars while seeking a verified outside delivery.

salt_recovery_009.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_009.text: The purchase plan's proposed seller had supplied a dated surplus statement after protecting its own local essential turns. That statement justified asking for a sale; it was not yet water in this reserve. The plan budgeted three forty-jar deliveries under separate carriage payments and current road checks. No household would have to pool its refund or disclose its private claim to fund them. The council's agreed commercial fund bore the purchase risk.

salt_recovery_010.speaker: an_ru
salt_recovery_010.text: 'If the outside delivery fails or its quality is refused, this plan still follows its local two-hundred-jar optional ceiling,' An Ru said. 'Do not write a larger entitlement against an order that has not arrived.' The cooperative accepted the condition. The reserve keeper added that accepted water would be counted once on receipt, after the required quality check. A seller's signature and a receiving measure had different jobs.

salt_recovery_011.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_011.text: The reserve floor and essential access rule bound every proposal. If usable spring yield fell or a new essential need consumed the contingency, optional draws stopped and the council received a dated notice. The corrected household turn book and refund receipts remained in force through that pause. A worker could question the chosen plan without losing a drinking turn. Yuan Lian asked the receiving officer to demonstrate the actual notice route before she signed.

salt_recovery_012.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_012.text: The officer brought a sample stop slip to the square, read it aloud and placed a copy at the grain house and cooperative. A carrier took another to the north-bank shelf. The sample was marked as a rehearsal, so nobody's tank was mistakenly closed. Su Lan timed the ordinary announcement and found that one landing shift could not hear it. They added the carrier route instead of sounding the bell harder.

salt_recovery_013.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_013.text: At dinner, Yue said she still wanted the fifth stage. Yuan Lian asked whether she could tell her next teacher what this month had taught. Yue began with a channel drawing, then spoke of Xiu's public report: a family could decline a visitor's questions and still collect its water. The forewoman listened. Opening more arm routes might one day enlarge her tasks. It would not let her choose someone else's acceptable cost without asking.

salt_recovery_014.speaker: narrator
salt_recovery_014.text: The final decision meeting opened with the actual trial balance, the twenty-one-day ceiling and a separate closure-day allowance. After the review, the twenty-fourth commission day would use five more reserve jars for essentials at the same conservative rate, with no optional work scheduled. Thus even the largest combined plan left at least one thousand forty at closure before contingency spending. The council could choose a limited course, observe it, and revise it at a dated meeting.

salt_final_choice.speaker: lin_yue
salt_final_choice.text: The council could adopt a common eighteen-day rotation, keep later optional tanks closed while paying eight maintenance shifts, or permit a smaller local draw beside a verified outside purchase. Each protected essential access, the reserve floor and the dated review. Each placed different costs on salt workers, seed growers and the reserve. Yue could accept the bounded work she would personally stay to do, then leave the remaining duties with named people who had agreed.

choices.text: Join the common water rotation and publish its actual draws.
Protect the reserve and join the paid maintenance shifts.
Audit a limited outside purchase with the local draw ceiling.

salt_rotation_001.speaker: narrator
salt_rotation_001.text: The common rotation began with signed turns and two blank columns: requested jars and actual jars. Yue worked beside Yuan Lian at the first noon count, then carried the posted result to the square. The spring met the conservative yield. The salt cooperative received its scheduled smaller turn only after the essential branches were filled. Nobody had to perform gratitude at the tap to make that order remain true.

salt_rotation_002.speaker: narrator
salt_rotation_002.text: On the fourth later day, the grain house asked for less water than its ceiling. The grain-house keeper's checked request stayed below the full seed allowance. Yuan Lian kept the unused jars in the reserve instead of offering them quietly to the cooperative. A salt worker protested, then read the common stop clause and asked the council to hear a revised request. Asking was permitted. Drawing before the reply was not.

salt_rotation_003.speaker: narrator
salt_rotation_003.text: The revised salt request failed one quality check, so its next turn stayed smaller. The cooperative shipped reduced-grade and raw sacks under their actual labels. Its price loss hurt. A worker left for one of the funded carrier shifts rather than accept the reduced washing hours. Yue helped him record the transfer without calling it disloyalty. A common plan did not require everyone to remain in the same job to prove it was common.

salt_rotation_004.speaker: narrator
salt_rotation_004.text: During the eighteen later days, actual optional use stopped at two hundred ten wash jars and fifty seed jars. That was below the three-hundred-forty ceiling. The reserve book retained each undrawn turn. Even with the largest possible ninety-jar early trial and the one-hundred-five essential shortfall, the review balance was at least eleven hundred twenty-five. No rain was credited. The protected contingency had not been needed to disguise an industrial overrun.

salt_rotation_005.speaker: narrator
salt_rotation_005.text: At the twenty-one-day water review, the clerk showed the corrected nineteen-household turns before the industrial totals. The supervisor's diversion case had its own evidence hearing and reply record; nobody used its unresolved sanction to postpone the existing credits. The council renewed essential access and set the next seasonal flow review. Yue signed only the completed work she had checked. Yuan Lian retained the operating duty after Yue's accepted hours ended.

salt_rotation_006.speaker: narrator
salt_rotation_006.text: The twenty-fourth commission day had no optional draw. Five further essential jars reduced the conservative lower bound to eleven hundred twenty at closure. The reserve keeper counted the actual balance and stored the measured result rather than substituting the lower bound for it. Wages and return fares were paid from their own accounts. Approved papers and equipment followed their recorded keepers, with no loan or extract made into a reward for staying.

salt_rotation_007.speaker: narrator
salt_rotation_007.text: At the north-bank shelf, a collector set down her jar without recognizing Yue at first. Then she asked when the next carrier came. Yue knew the named turn and showed it on the board. The woman thanked her for that answer, not for the valley's old story. Yue walked to the cart with her fourth-stage cord under her sleeve.
