A useful month could end without making her the keeper of every morning after it.

salt_end_rotation.speaker: narrator
salt_end_rotation.text: Yuan Lian read the noon measure after Yue's cart had gone. The ordinary spring wheel turned; a reduced salt batch waited for its accepted turn. Nineteen restored households kept their tokens and their questions. On the porch, the forewoman left room beside the actual count for tomorrow's correction. Yue had helped make that room easier to use. It belonged to the people who would still be standing beside it.

salt_maintenance_001.speaker: narrator
salt_maintenance_001.text: The reserve-first plan kept later optional tanks closed. The salt cooperative sold the available raw stock and recorded the missed refined order as a price loss. The grain house issued its safe dry-sorted seed and retained any trial salvage under its separate label. Eight temporary maintenance shifts were funded from the access account. They were actual offers at stated rates, not a claim that every lost washing shift had been replaced.

salt_maintenance_002.speaker: narrator
salt_maintenance_002.text: Yue accepted three of the eight shifts and left the others to workers who chose them. On the first, she helped a carpenter replace the north-bank shelf's temporary prop with an inspected ordinary support. The carrier tested the loaded shelf while the carpenter watched the joint. A woman waiting with two jars asked who would fix it next time. Yuan Lian pointed to the maintenance receiver's posted name and the remaining fund.

salt_maintenance_003.speaker: narrator
salt_maintenance_003.text: The second shift repaired carrier straps and fitted spare wheel pegs into labelled tool bags. Yue wanted to add one more unpaid evening to finish a prettier case for the pegs. Xiu said the bags already kept the tools dry and asked whether that evening belonged to rest or duties actually recorded on Yue's appointment page. Yue laughed at how easily useful work could become an excuse to postpone something less flattering.

salt_maintenance_004.speaker: narrator
salt_maintenance_004.text: On the third shift, the qualified mason documented the buried approach's future support repair without opening the far reed bank. The commission had funded inspection and a limited near repair, not every excavation on his drawing. He priced the next work separately. Yue left the uncured future mortar off the present safety report and helped replace the warning cord. The road remained useful on its checked route while the hollow board stayed closed.

salt_maintenance_005.speaker: narrator
salt_maintenance_005.text: At the water review, no later optional jars had been drawn. The reserve's conservative lower bound was thirteen hundred eighty-five after essential demand and the largest possible early trial. Actual balances depended on the chosen experiment and stood separately in the book. The council had bought more reserve time at the cost of paused industrial work. It named that cost before asking workers about the next seasonal plan.

salt_maintenance_006.speaker: narrator
salt_maintenance_006.text: The closure day drew five further essential jars, leaving a lower bound of thirteen hundred eighty without contingency spending. The eight funded shifts were complete, with the unfinished larger repair priced on another sheet. The commission paid Yue's earned wages and return fare. Accepted orchard correspondence stayed with its actual appointment owner; a requested new date was not marked completed merely because the messenger had been paid.

salt_maintenance_007.speaker: narrator
salt_maintenance_007.text: Before departure, Yue carried one full jar up the north stair at the collector's requested pace. The shelf and paid route would carry future turns after she left. She set the jar down and felt her ordinary arms ache. Her fourth stage had not opened a leg pair or removed the hill. The collector handed her an empty cup for the journey and said that she hoped the next visit could begin with tea.

salt_end_maintenance.speaker: narrator
salt_end_maintenance.text: On the departing cart, Yue listened to the empty cup knock softly against her bedding. The valley still needed a new season's decision. Its reserve now gave that decision a longer interval, and its carriers had tools they could find. She kept the paid shift tally beside her practice sheet, neither replacing the other. Ahead lay further opened routes if she could earn them. Behind lay ordinary work completed within the hours she had actually promised.
salt_end_maintenance.ending: A Cup for the Next Visit

salt_purchase_001.speaker: narrator
salt_purchase_001.text: The limited purchase plan opened no larger local ceiling while the external order travelled. Yue and An Ru checked the seller's certified surplus statement and the receiving contract at separate desks. The seller's own protected household turns came first; the sale covered forty surplus jars on each of three specified days. Their document review justified the order. It did not authorize drawing water from a village that had not made that offer.

salt_purchase_002.speaker: narrator
salt_purchase_002.text: The first delivery arrived on two checked freight carts, with listed jar seals. A qualified inspector tested the water under the valley's drinking criteria before clean storage accepted it. One loose cover had collected road dust; those ten litres stayed outside the accepted count. The receiving contract required the seller to supply the replacement and pay its extra carriage. The carrier received payment for the actual journey. A refusal needed a funded receiving route, not a reassuring explanation.

salt_purchase_003.speaker: narrator
salt_purchase_003.text: Yue wanted to accept the replacement on the driver's promise because the other jars had passed. An Ru kept the first receiving count at thirty-nine accepted jars. The promise entered an owed-quantity column. The two later forty-jar deliveries passed their own checks, and the replacement arrived under a fourth checked carriage record charged to the seller. Only then did accepted outside supply reach one hundred twenty jars. The council's carriage budget still paid only the three agreed deliveries.

salt_purchase_004.speaker: narrator
salt_purchase_004.text: The salt cooperative received at most one hundred eighty later wash jars, and the grain house at most twenty. The local optional ceiling remained two hundred even after the purchase arrived. The council retained the received water as reserve against future essential demand rather than treating it as an invitation to expand every industrial request. A buyer could disagree with that choice at the review. No warehouse door could alter it privately.

salt_purchase_005.speaker: narrator
salt_purchase_005.text: An Ru published water quantity, carriage cost, quality refusals and receiving dates without the households' private refund balances. The eighty-four copper from the old diversion had been restored to its own credit account; nobody was required to spend it on this purchase. The grain house separately credited verified zero-wash surcharges. A customer taking her refund home left the square just as freely as one who chose to buy an additional jar.

salt_purchase_006.speaker: narrator
salt_purchase_006.text: At the review, the local conservative lower bound was eleven hundred eighty-five after essential demand, the largest early trial and the two-hundred-jar later ceiling. One hundred twenty actually accepted purchased jars raised that bound to thirteen hundred five. The closure day's five essential jars left at least thirteen hundred without contingency spending. The measured balance stood above the calculation, with the completed supplier obligation and four carriage receipts distinguishing the seller-paid replacement.

salt_purchase_007.speaker: narrator
salt_purchase_007.text: On closure morning, the driver asked whether Yue could recommend him for the next season. She described the journeys she had witnessed and the rejected cover he had helped replace. She could not promise the next commission's contract. He accepted the limited recommendation, tucked it under his strap and checked the wheel peg before leaving. Yue collected her own paid fare afterward, glad that both departures had records ordinary enough to be believed.

salt_end_purchase.speaker: narrator
salt_end_purchase.text: An Ru filed the purchase packet beside the corrected turn book, leaving the old descriptions visible under their amendments. The water existed because a source had offered a bounded surplus, carriers had brought it, and someone had refused a dirty cover before counting it. Yue left with the copy she was actually permitted to keep. The valley's reserve held more time. No signature in the archive pretended to own the rain.
